description: Modern Physics and Radioactivity under General Science deals with the study of atoms, nuclei, and their radiation. It is crucial for understanding subatomic particles, quantum phenomena, and energy transformations for competitive exams.

sections.title: Atomic Structure and Fundamental Particles
sections.description: Overview of the basic structure of an atom and its subatomic constituents.

key_concepts.explanation: The smallest unit of matter, consisting of a dense, positively charged central nucleus surrounded by orbiting negatively charged electrons.
Atoms of the same element having the same atomic number (number of protons) but a different mass number (number of neutrons).
Atoms of different elements having the same mass number but different atomic numbers.

key_associations.extra_info: Negatively charged particle, discovered via cathode ray tube experiments.
Positively charged particle residing inside the atomic nucleus.
Neutral particle with no electric charge, located inside the nucleus.
The antiparticle of the electron, carrying a positive charge.

important_facts.fact: The nucleus of an atom was discovered by Ernest Rutherford through his famous Gold Foil (Alpha scattering) experiment.

sections.title: Radioactivity and Decay
sections.description: The process of spontaneous emission of radiation from unstable atomic nuclei.

key_concepts.explanation: The spontaneous emission of radiation (alpha, beta, or gamma) from the unstable nucleus of a heavy element to achieve stability.
The time required for a quantity of a radioactive substance to decay to exactly half of its initial value.

historical_events.significance: Henri Becquerel accidentally discovered radioactivity in uranium salts.
Marie Curie and Pierre Curie discovered these highly radioactive elements from pitchblende ore.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: In Alpha decay, atomic number decreases by 2 and mass number by 4. In Beta decay, atomic number increases by 1 with no change in mass number.
scientific_principles.application: Used to trace the creation of new elements in a radioactive decay chain.

key_associations.extra_info: Positively charged, lowest penetrating power, highest ionizing power. Blocked by a sheet of paper.
Negatively charged, moderate penetrating power. Blocked by aluminum foil.
Neutral (no charge), travel at the speed of light, highest penetrating power. Blocked by thick lead.

important_facts.fact: The SI unit of radioactivity is the Becquerel (Bq), while the traditional unit is the Curie (Ci).

sections.title: Photoelectric Effect and Quantum Theory
sections.description: Study of the dual nature of light and the quantization of energy.

key_concepts.explanation: The phenomenon of emission of electrons from a metal surface when light of a suitable threshold frequency falls on it.
A discrete bundle (quantum) of electromagnetic light energy having zero rest mass.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: K_max = hv - W (where K_max is max kinetic energy, hv is photon energy, and W is work function).
scientific_principles.application: Fundamental principle behind the working of solar panels, photocells, and light sensors.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: E = hv (Energy = Planck's constant x frequency).
scientific_principles.application: Explains black body radiation and atomic emission spectra.

important_facts.fact: Albert Einstein was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921 for his theoretical explanation of the photoelectric effect, not for the theory of relativity.

sections.title: Nuclear Energy and Reactions
sections.description: Principles governing the immense energy released during nuclear fission and fusion.

key_concepts.explanation: The process where a heavy, unstable nucleus splits into two or more lighter nuclei when bombarded with slow-moving neutrons, releasing massive energy.
The process where two or more light nuclei combine at extremely high temperatures and pressures to form a single, heavier nucleus.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: E = mc^2 (Energy = mass x speed of light squared).
scientific_principles.application: Explains the massive energy release in nuclear reactors and atomic weapons due to mass defect.

key_associations.extra_info: Based on an uncontrolled nuclear chain reaction; developed by J. Robert Oppenheimer (Manhattan Project).
Significantly more powerful than the atomic bomb; developed by Edward Teller.
Used in a nuclear reactor to absorb excess neutrons and control the fission chain reaction.
Used to slow down fast-moving neutrons so they can effectively trigger further fission.

important_facts.fact: Nuclear fusion is the primary source of immense energy in the Sun and other stars.
Apsara, established in 1956 at the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), was India's and Asia's first nuclear reactor.
